data.positioning_title: Where M-886 Fits in Product Evaluation
positioning_paragraphs: M-886 is a rutile titanium dioxide pigment for plastics produced by the chloride process.

Its documented public profile covers polyolefin masterbatch, high-temperature extrusion and cast-film processing, and engineering plastics. Use M-886 as an evaluation candidate when dispersion, bright-white color direction and processing behavior are relevant. Final Grade selection should account for the polymer, carrier resin, additive package, pigment loading, processing temperature, equipment, end-use requirements and destination-document needs.

data.applications_title: Plastics and Masterbatch Directions to Evaluate

applications.title: Polyolefin Masterbatches
applications.text: Evaluate M-886 at the intended pigment loading and carrier-resin system. Confirm dispersion, color direction, processing behavior and downstream dilution performance under the actual masterbatch conditions.

applications.title: High-Temperature Extrusion and Cast-Film Processing
applications.text: Review M-886 under the intended high-temperature extrusion and cast-film conditions. Confirm dispersion, color, film appearance, processing stability and melt-flow behavior in the complete polymer formulation.

applications.title: Engineering Plastics
applications.text: Include M-886 in engineering-plastics testing using the actual polymer, additives, pigment loading, processing temperature and equipment. Confirm appearance, dispersion, processing behavior and end-use suitability.

data.evaluation_title: What to Evaluate in Your Plastics Formulation

evaluation.title: Dispersion and Appearance Review
items: Dispersion behavior at the intended pigment loading and mixing conditions
Bright-white color direction in the complete formulation
Finished appearance in the selected polymer system
Color and dispersion consistency after downstream processing

evaluation.title: Processing and Qualification Review
items: Melt-flow behavior under the intended formulation and processing conditions
High-temperature extrusion or cast-film conditions, where applicable
Compatibility with the selected resin, carrier and additive package
End-use requirements, destination-document needs and sample-validation results
